Nearest City: Portland, OR
Incident Type: FIXED
Material: GROUND WATER, AND MACHINE COOLANT MIXTURE
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: BOEING
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 36000 gallons

THE CAUSE OF THE ORIGINAL LEAK IS UNKNOWN AT THIS TIME.

Reported Spill Volume: 79 gallon
Report DescriptionCALLER REPORTS A SPILL OF 300 L OF DIESEL FROM A 352 EXCAVATOR DUE TO A MECHANICAL FAILURE (FROZEN LINE). AT THE TIME, THEY WERE TRYING TO REMOVE AN OLD, ABANDONED BOX CULVERT WHICH WAS UNDER THE ROAD WHEN THE SPILL OCCURRED. THE SPILL LANDED ON A HEAVILY COMPACTED FROZEN CLAY BASE. NO STORM SEWERS, CATCH BASINS OR WATERWAYS WERE IMPACTED. PADS AND BOOMS WERE PLACED AROUND THE GROUND AND GRANULAR ABSORBENT. THE AREA WAS BERMED AS WELL TO PREVENT THE DIESEL FROM MIGRATING. THE CONTAMINATED SOIL IS CURRENTLY BEING REMOVED BY AN EXCAVATOR. THE MATERIAL WILL THEN BE TRANSFERRED INTO A LINED DISPOSAL BIN. CALLER INDICATES THAT HE IS WATCHING THE DIESEL AND IT HAS NOT IMPACTED THE DETROIT RIVER WHICH IS 50 METRES AWAY. THE EXCAVATOR IS BEING REPAIRED AND SOIL SAMPLES WILL BE TAKEN. CALLER ANTICIPATES THE CLEANUP TO BE FINISHED IN AN HOUR AND WILL UPDATE SAC WHEN THIS OCCURS.

Report Description///POTENTIAL RELEASE REPORT/// ///CRITICAL INCIDENT COMMUNICATIONS (CIC) REPORT - INITIAL - F/V ARCTIC SEA - AGROUND VESSEL WITH 9 POB IVO ST. GEORGE ISLAND, AK - 05 JAN 2026/// INITIAL INCIDENT TYPE: MASS RESCUE OPERATION LOCATION: ST. GEORGE ISLAND, ALASKA TIME INCIDENT OCCURRED: 0812 EST / 1312Z, 05JAN2026 TIME OF INITIAL REPORT TO NCC: 1350 EST / 1850Z, 05JAN2026 NAME OF REPORTING UNIT: USCG ARCTIC DISTRICT INITIAL: • ON JANUARY 5TH, FISHING VESSEL (F/V) ARCTIC SEA WAS DISABLED AND RAN AGROUND ON THE NORTH SIDE OF ST. GEORGE ISLAND, ALASKA. • HER SISTER SHIP, F/V NORTH SEA WAS ABLE TO BROADCAST THE INFORMATION TO USCG ARCTIC DISTRICT. • AFTER THE F/V ARCTIC SEA RAN AGROUND, THE VESSEL BEGAN TAKING ON WATER. • DUE TO RUNNING AGROUND, THE FLOODING OF THE VESSEL HAS STOPPED AND HAS NOT PROGRESSED ABOVE THE WATERLINE. • THERE ARE NINE CREWMEMBERS ONBOARD, AND THEY HAVE ALL DONNED SURVIVAL SUITS, INFLATED THEIR LIFE RAFT, AND ACTIVATED THEIR EPIRB. • THE CREW MEMBERS HAVE NOT ABANDONED SHIP AND BELIEVE THEY ARE IN NO DANGER OF CAPSIZING. • A COAST GUARD HELICOPTER FROM USCG AIR STATION KODIAK (CG-6035) IS ENROUTE TO THE F/V ARCTIC SEA WITH AN ANTICIPATED ARRIVAL TIME OF 1450 EST / 1950Z. • A COAST GUARD C-130 IS ON SCENE AND MAINTAINING RADIO COMMUNICATION WITH THE F/V ARCTIC SEA EVERY 30 MINUTES. • CG-6035 INTENDS TO HOIST ALL NINE CREWMEMBERS WITHIN THE SAME SORTIE AND TRANSPORT THEM TO ST. PAUL MEDICAL CENTER. • ON SCENE WEATHER HAS THE WINDS COMING OUT OF THE NORTH-NORTHWEST AT 25 KNOTS, SEAS ARE FOUR FEET, WITH HALF A MILE OF VISIBILITY. • THE CIC PROCESS WAS STOOD DOWN WITH CONCURRENCE FROM BOTH AREAS. • NCC WILL PROVIDE AN EMAIL UPDATE ONCE ALL NINE CREWMEMBERS ARE HOISTED AND SAFELY ABOARD CG-6035.

STARTING AT APPROXIMATELY 0600 HOURS, FLOOD WATERS ROSE ONTO THE SERVICE CENTER PROPERTY. BY 0800 HOURS, THERE WAS APPROXIMATELY FOUR FEET OF WATER OVER OUR PROPERTY AND INTO OUR SERVICE BUILDING. BY APPROXIMATELY 1530 HOURS, THE FLOOD WATER HAD MOSTLY RECEDED. AT THIS TIME, WHILE ASSESSING DAMAGE TO THE PROPERTY, A HEAVY SHEEN OF OIL (MOST LIKELY AUTOMOTIVE TYPE OILS) WAS OBSERVED INSIDE OF THE BUILDING ON THE REMAINING WATER. A SHEEN OF OIL WAS OBSERVED OUTSIDE THE BUILDING (ASSOCIATED WITH THE OIL RELEASE OBSERVED INSIDE THE BUILDING). SUNPRO, A LOCAL SPILL CLEANUP CONTRACTOR, HAS BEEN CALLED IN TO CONTAIN AND CLEANUP THE RELEASED MATERIALS. THE MATERIALS WERE ORIGINALLY STORED ON SHELVING IN A LOW LYING WORK/TOOL STORAGE AREA.
